title: Anatomy of the Lambda Expression
description: Understand lambda expressions, the building blocks of LINQ method syntax, and how to use them effectively.

data.text: C# 3.0 (.NET 3.5) introduced the **lambda expression** along with LINQ. The lambda expression is a shorter way of representing anonymous methods using special syntax.
From Anonymous Methods to Lambda Expressions
Consider the following anonymous method that checks if a student is a teenager:
The same logic can be expressed as a lambda expression:
Lambda Expression Evolution
The lambda expression evolves from the anonymous method by:

items: Removing the `delegate` keyword and parameter type
Removing curly braces, `return`, and semicolon for single expressions
Removing parentheses when there is only one parameter

data.caption: Evolution from anonymous method to lambda expression

    B --> C[s => s.Age > 12]

terms.definition: A concise way to represent anonymous methods using the => operator.
A delegate that takes input parameters and returns a value. The last type parameter is the return type.
A delegate that takes input parameters but does not return a value.
A delegate that takes a parameter and returns a boolean value.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Lambda expressions are concise anonymous methods using the => operator
They can have zero, one, or multiple parameters
Multiple statements require curly braces and explicit return
Lambda expressions can be assigned to Func, Action, and Predicate delegates
They are the foundation of LINQ method syntax
